claims.text: High-thermal-load additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components produces significant residual thermal stresses.
The as-manufactured AlCrFeNiSi components have degraded mechanical properties.
The as-manufactured AlCrFeNiSi components contain complex microstructural defects.
Heat treatment at 800–850°C for approximately one hour promotes stress relaxation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Heat treatment at 800–850°C for approximately one hour promotes recrystallization in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Immediate liquid-nitrogen quenching after heat treatment locks in the improved microstructure.
The two-stage treatment reduces dislocation density in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
The two-stage treatment reduces internal stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
The two-stage treatment causes grain refinement and/or controlled recrystallization.
Reduced dislocation density, reduced internal stress, and modified grain structure mediate improved yield strength and ductility.
High-temperature treatment activates diffusion processes in AlCrFeNiSi.
The thermally activated diffusion processes permit recrystallization.
The thermally activated diffusion processes relieve internal stresses.
Rapid cryogenic quenching prevents undesirable grain growth after heat treatment.
The treated components will have lower residual thermal stresses than components made by the same high-thermal-load AM process without post-processing.
The treated components will have higher yield strength than untreated controls.
The treated components will have greater ductility than untreated controls.
The treated components will exhibit a more favorable microstructure than untreated controls.
